s1.syndrome_frame: subacute pulmonary syndrome with weight loss and persistent cough
salient_findings: coarse crepitations over the right upper and lower lung zones
air-space opacity in the right upper lobe on chest radiograph
key_facts: 56-year-old woman
no significant medical history
denies fever, haemoptysis, night sweats
no known contacts with tuberculosis
two courses of antibiotics produced no improvement
coarse crepitations heard over the right upper and lower lung zones
chest radiograph showed an air-space opacity in the right upper lobe
CT of the thorax demonstrated multifocal consolidations in the right upper lobe extending to the right lower lobe
symptoms persisted after 2 weeks of empirical anti-tuberculosis therapy
Mantoux tuberculin skin test showed 10 mm of induration
sputum induction for acid-fast bacilli was negative
bronchoalveolar lavage was negative for Xpert Mycobacterium tuberculosis/rifampicin assay and bacterial and fungal cultures

shortlist.why_kept: persistent cough and weight loss with negative infectious workup

shortlist.why_kept: subacute pulmonary syndrome with weight loss and persistent cough

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of dry cough and mild weight loss, lack of response to antibiotics, and radiographic findings of multifocal consolidations are consistent with organizing pneumonia. The negative tests for tuberculosis and other infections also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: While possible, the lack of other systemic symptoms and the specific radiographic pattern make it less likely

rejected.label: Lymphangitic carcinomatosis
rejected.why: There is no mention of a known malignancy or other symptoms suggestive of metastatic disease

rejected.label: Bronchoalveolar cell carcinoma
rejected.why: The radiographic findings and clinical presentation are not typical for this type of cancer

rejected.label: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis
rejected.why: There is no clear exposure history to suggest an allergic reaction to an inhaled antigen
